transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Sofia Ramos (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Platform Lead, NexaRetail), Marcus Lee (CTO), Elena Gomez (Security), Jamal Ortiz (ML Eng)

Summary: Kickoff to align on POC activation gates: access, workload samples, benchmark metrics, mid-point review and final exec readout. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/KMS needs, and a tight 4-week timeline with a mid-point technical checkpoint.

00:00:05 Sofia Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45-60 minutes, quick intros — I'm Sofia, AE, Liam is our SE, we'll drive the POC ops and the bench plan.
00:00:22 Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. We're trying to validate low-latency routing for our checkout recommendation service and measure cost/throughput. Marcus and Elena will chime in on infra and security.
00:00:36 Marcus Lee: Hey. We're also looking for an exec-ready readout — CTO-level summary and a go/no-go recommendation. Targeting Q3 deployment if POC hits goals.
00:00:50 Liam Chen: Great. Quick question on current infra — are you running inference on-prem, cloud, or hybrid? And what traffic shape do you expect?
00:01:05 Jamal Ortiz: We're mostly GCP today, some on-prem for PCI stuff. Peak concurrent requests around 150 rps during promos, average 25 rps. Typical prompt length ~120 tokens, but some sessions with long contexts to ~2k tokens for personalization.
00:01:27 Sofia Ramos: Good, that gives us a starting point. For the POC we'll want a 48-hour representative trace and a smaller 1-hour burst trace. That helps us configure batching and KV cache behavior.
00:01:45 Elena Gomez: Security — we need to understand data residency and key management. Do you support customer-managed keys and VPC peering for dedicated?
00:02:01 Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and VPC options; for Hosted we offer encryption in transit and at rest but can integrate with KMS in Dedicated/Private. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
00:02:20 Priya Nair: Timeline question — can we do a 3-week POC or do you recommend 4 weeks with the mid-point review?
00:02:33 Sofia Ramos: For the scope you described (representative traffic + exec readout), we recommend 4 weeks: week 0 access and onboarding, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 tuning and mid-point review, week 3 final runs and exec prep. We can compress but that risks missing scale tuning.
00:02:56 Marcus Lee: What's baseline we should expect for latency? Our SLO is p95 < 250ms for single-turn recommendations.
00:03:10 Liam Chen: It depends heavily on model and deployment mode. For a 7B family open model on Redwood Hosted with batching, we've seen p95 in 120-300ms depending on sequence length. On Dedicated with optimized kernels and bigger GPUs, you can push p95 lower but cost rises. We'll put ranges in the benchmark plan.
00:03:34 Jamal Ortiz: About cost — can you give a rough per-1M token estimate for hosted vs dedicated?
00:03:44 Sofia Ramos: We'll provide an estimated band. Hosted typically has higher per-token rate but no infra ops overhead. Dedicated is lower marginal token cost but requires committed capacity. We can show break-even points based on your RPS and token distribution.
00:03:58 Priya Nair: Success criteria — we want three concrete checks: 1) p95 latency <250ms for 90% of traffic, 2) cost per 1M tokens under X (customer to set X), 3) integration with our SSO + KMS and ability to run in VPC. Does that align?
00:04:25 Sofia Ramos: Yes, those are good. We'll translate into measurable metrics in the POC plan.
00:04:33 Elena Gomez: We'll need SOC2 documentation and a sample SLAs doc. Also audit log format — do you have structured event logs?
00:04:46 Liam Chen: We do. We can share SOC2 summary and sample audit logs; logs include token-level request metadata, model version, and route. Note that in some cases names of fields in the export might be abbreviated or slightly different.
00:05:02 Priya Nair: For access, do you need VPN/VPC peering or can we use temporary IP allowlist?
00:05:13 Sofia Ramos: Both are possible. For the initial benchmark, an IP allowlist and API key is fastest. If you need private connectivity we can provision VPC peering in parallel; that usually takes a few days to schedule with network teams.
00:05:28 Marcus Lee: On observability, we need per-route token cost breakdown. Is that in Redwood Console?
00:05:36 Liam Chen: Yes, the Console exposes token-level cost by route/model and latency histograms. For the POC we'll grant access to a read-only dashboard.
00:05:48 Jamal Ortiz: About the mid-point review — what do you typically present?
00:05:54 Sofia Ramos: At mid-point we'll show baseline vs tuned runs: latency p50/p95, throughput at target concurrency, cost per token estimates, and a list of tuning actions (batch sizes, quantization suggestions). If there are blockers we'll escalate.
00:06:12 Priya Nair: Any gotchas with long-context sessions and KV caching?
00:06:18 Liam Chen: Long contexts change memory pressure and KV cache hit rates. We'll instrument cache hit stats and may recommend prefix caching for user sessions to reduce repeated token compute. Sometimes transcripts show "KV cash" in old notes but that's just a transcribe issue.
00:06:35 Elena Gomez: Data retention — can you TTL logs at our retention policy?
00:06:40 Liam Chen: Yes, retention and log export can be configured; we'll add the retention config doc.
00:06:52 Sofia Ramos: Ok, let's align on concrete deliverables. We'll need: 1) sample traces and traffic profile from Jamal, 2) security requirements from Elena, 3) decision on Hosted vs Dedicated preliminary preference from Marcus/Priya.
00:07:10 Jamal Ortiz: I'll upload traces and sample prompts to the shared folder.
00:07:15 Priya Nair: We prefer hosted to start but open to Dedicated if cost numbers justify.
00:07:21 Marcus Lee: Agreed. We want to avoid upfront commits unless the delta is compelling.
00:07:28 Sofia Ramos: Noted. We'll model break-even and show it in the pricing band.
00:07:34 Liam Chen: For the benchmark plan I'll propose these test cases: steady-state throughput at 25 rps, peak burst at 150 rps, long-context sessions with 2k tokens, and a cold-start latency test. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and token cost.
00:07:56 Priya Nair: Sounds good. Can you also test a fallback policy if the model is rate-limited, like routing to a cheaper model for non-critical recommendations?
00:08:07 Liam Chen: Yes, smart routing is supported in Redwood. We'll include a run that exercises fallback to a smaller model and measure end-to-end degradation.
00:08:18 Elena Gomez: For compliance sign-off we need to see dataflow diagrams and where keys are held.
00:08:25 Sofia Ramos: We'll attach a simplified dataflow diagram and an infra reachability map.
00:08:33 Marcus Lee: Who will present at the exec readout?
00:08:37 Sofia Ramos: Typically our AE + your Platform lead present a 15-20 minute exec summary, with metrics and cost/benefit. We can prep a slide deck template for you.
00:08:49 Priya Nair: Mid-point review — we prefer to invite an engineering manager and the head of product.
00:08:56 Sofia Ramos: Great, please add them to the invite for the mid-point.
00:09:03 Jamal Ortiz: Quick nit: do you have any standard load generator or do we supply the harness?
00:09:10 Liam Chen: We'll provide a lightweight test harness and scripts; if you want deterministic replay of traces you can provide them and we'll run them in our bench infra.
00:09:22 Priya Nair: Any other dependencies?
00:09:25 Sofia Ramos: Network whitelisting, API keys, and optionally VPC peering. We'll email a checklist that covers ports, CIDR, and required IAM roles.
00:09:35 Elena Gomez: One more — what's your policy on model artifacts? We need assurance models won't be persisted on third-party storage.
00:09:44 Liam Chen: Model weights are managed by Redwood; customer data is not used to train public models by default. We can sign a data use attestation in the contract.
00:09:58 Sofia Ramos: Ok, time check — we've covered the main gates. To recap: onboarding/access, sample traces, baseline runs, mid-point tuning, final runs and exec. We'll send a formal POC plan doc and the onboarding checklist after this call.
00:10:13 Marcus Lee: Good. If we hit the p95 target and cost bands look reasonable, procurement will fast-track Dedicated discussions.
00:10:22 Priya Nair: When can we get the benchmark plan?
00:10:26 Liam Chen: I'll share a draft by 2025-06-17.
00:10:30 Sofia Ramos: I'll send the onboarding checklist and SOC2 summary by EOD 2025-06-12.
00:10:36 Priya Nair: Thanks, that works.
00:10:40 Sofia Ramos: Any last questions?
00:10:44 Elena Gomez: Nothing else.
00:10:46 Jamal Ortiz: All good.
00:10:48 Sofia Ramos: Great, we'll follow up with links to the shared drive, the bench harness repo, and the draft benchmark plan.
00:10:55 Priya Nair: Thanks everyone.
00:10:58 Sofia Ramos: Thanks — talk soon.

End notes: Shared artifacts referenced during call: POC onboarding checklist (link in follow-up), benchmark plan (to be shared), SOC2 summary and sample audit logs (to be shared), bench harness repo (link).

Action items recap: see action_items above. Mid-point review tentatively scheduled week of 2025-07-07. Exec readout to be scheduled after final runs (target late July).
